title: The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model
main_claim: For the nearest-neighbour cosine XY model on Z^2 at b_c, the free-box thermodynamic two-point function satisfies C_{b_c}(r) = B_XY r^{-1/4} (log r)^{1/8} (1+o(1)) with B_XY in (0,inf). The proof goes through the centre magnetisation M_n ~ b_M n^{-1/8} (log n)^{1/16} and the ratio C/M_r^2 -> c_shape.

issues.location: Introduction (route) and Section 3 geometry, Section 5 trajectory, Section 6 observable; references to companions C, B, S
issues.description: This is not a gap in this paper. The theorem depends heavily on unaudited companion results: a(b_c)=8pi and the four-face phase estimate (C), the analytic local maps and contraction Prop 8.3 / Eq. 8.17-8.18 / Lemma 8.1 (B), and the sector costs and annular kernels (S). The fixed-geometry comparison (Prop geo:comparison) and the cutoff entry section (about 2500 lines) could only be skimmed. Correctness at that level is assumed, not verified.
issues.evidence: "We use from that paper the critical height coefficient a(b_c)=8pi, finite Bessel comparisons, fixed-geometry and conditional height limits, and a four-face characteristic estimate. The analytic local maps come from [B], and the sector costs ... from [S]."

coverage: I read the introduction, the full conclusion (proof of Thm 1.1), the statement of Prop obs:consecutive and the proof of the Green constant, the statement of Prop trj:trajectory and its analytic setup, and the overlap lemma plus the whole dyadic-switch barrier/separatrix argument (trajectory.tex lines 1020-1364). I skimmed the geometry and cutoff-entry sections; they are too long for line-by-line checking. Checked by hand: -(1-t)/(2a)(2*pi*l + Dc) with a=8pi and t=1/(2lN) gives -l/8 + 1/(16N) - Dc/(16pi) + Dc/(32 pi l N), which matches eq. magnetization-increment. Error terms N^{-2+4eps} + N^{-1-eps} are summable for 0<eps<1/10. The summation-by-parts identity is correct. g_n = 4pi^2 G_n(0,0) = 2pi l N + c, where the continuum dyadic diagonal is log2/(2pi). The marginal eigenvalue L^{-2t} gives b_* = 2 log L. Both barrier inequalities follow correctly from the sampled bounds. I_j = u^2 - c0^2 Y^2 has cancelling leading increments. 1/Y_j = b_* c0 j + O(log j) is consistent with O(log j) switches each carrying an O(1) error, and it gives u_j = 1/(b_* j) + O(log j / j^2) with absolute index j. Window compatibility holds: j' = N - O(log N) lies in [c2^k, c'2^k] for N in [2^k, 2^{k+1}). The extension from geometric sizes to all n, and the squaring to (log r)^{1/8}, are correct. The sign and power of the log correction agree with the KT/Janke prediction.
